jin: Heads-up — saw a regression that looks tied to kernel-pick behavior for medium seqs (roughly 384-768).
jin: Baseline: before autotune, seq=512 batch=4 used kernel=matmul_v1 on arm64 and had stable p50/p95. After last autotune rollout it picks matmul_v2 and p95 jumped ~15%.
jin: Quick repro: `./run_infer --model=redwood-l2 --seq=512 --batch=4 --warmup=50`
jin: Example debug log (KERNEL_PICK_DEBUG=1):
```
PICK_LOG: {"chosen":"matmul_v2","scores":{"matmul_v1":0.43,"matmul_v2":0.55,"matmul_simd":0.02},"reason_tags":["arch:arm64","seq_bucket:512","simd_preference:neon"],"kv_cache_hit":false}
```
noah: Oof, thanks. Do we have perf traces for matmul_v1 vs v2 at seq=512? can you attach a flamegraph?
jin: Attached quick perf link: https://internal.perf/fg/2409/seq512-mv1-vs-mv2 (sandboxed).
noah: Looking at the traces, v2 has extra memory copies and a different tiling for seq ~512, which explains the extra latency. It was tuned for long sequences >1024.
anya: This is the classic seq-dependent path flip. Autotuner learned a slight aggregate win but didn't tag the seq-range strongly. We need the telemetry to include the tuner confidence and the training_sample_distribution.
anya: Proposal: send these additional fields from runtime when KERNEL_PICK_DEBUG=1: `chosen_kernel`, `candidate_scores`, `seq_len_bucket`, `cpu_microarch`, `simd_width`, `batch_size`, `kv_cache_hit`, `tuner_confidence` and `autotune_model_version`.
daphne: Agree. Also add an alert rule to detect >10% p95 regressions bucketed by seq_len_bucket and kernel. We can canary the autotune change too.
perf-bot: Perf profile captured for thread 2409012345: run_id=pf-2409-01, cpu=arm64-a510, p50=72ms, p95=195ms, chosen=matmul_v2
jin: Repro steps I'm going to run on canary: 1) rollback autotune config that prefers v2 for seq in [256,768] 2) run 2k requests @batch4 seq512 3) collect pick logs + profiles
inja: (note: ninja is offline)
off-topic aside: please ignore above
noah: We should also instrument kv-cache interactions: I noticed kv_cache_hit=false in most failed traces — maybe cold cache is amplifying the memory copy cost. If we see kv_hit=true, v2 might be fine. Add `kv_prefetch_status` to telemetry.
anya: Good call. I'll add an autotune safety rule: only accept kernel flips if tuner_confidence>0.8 OR candidate_improvement_margin>0.12 for the target seq_bucket AND kv_cache_hit distribution stable.
daphne: For rollout: canary 1% traffic in us-west1 for 2 hours, collect p50/p95 by seq_bucket and chosen_kernel. If p95 delta >8% rollback.
jin: I'll open a PR for the extra debug env flag and telemetry fields. Draft name: `KERNEL_PICK_SAMPLING=1` with payload schema attached in PR.
noah: Can you paste the minimal log schema here? I want to ensure logging size is bounded.
jin: Minimal schema (stringified JSON per request): `{"ts","req_id","model","seq_len","batch","chosen_kernel","scores","seq_bucket","cpu","kv_hit","tuner_confidence"}`. Keep optional large arrays (scores) sampled at 1/100 unless KERNEL_PICK_DEBUG=1.
anya: Also include `runtime_flags` array so we know when prefetch or aggressive-batch is on.
ninja2: +1 to sampling. We don't want to explode logs.
perf-bot: Telemetry quota note: current sampling budget allows ~0.5% at 99th percentile RPS for eng accounts.
daphne: Action items: jin PR for flag + schema, anya update autotuner rules, noah run perf comparison, ops add canary alert, collect 2h dataset.
jin: I'll tag the PR `eng-runtime/kpick-debug-2409` and set to collect for 2 hours then auto-turn-off.
noah: After we collect data, let's run the offline tuner simulation to see if a constrained autotune (seq-aware) would have chosen v1 for 512.
anya: I'll do the simulation once PR lands.
daphne: Sweet. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
jin: I'll post results here once the 2h run finishes.
perf-bot: Canary started: sample_rate=0.01, region=us-west1, start=2409015600
